commits.author: ravwojdyla-agent
commits.message:
[ci] Fix native floor bumps under uv 0.13.9 and for extra floors (#12001)

The native package floor updater has failed on every run since uv 0.13.9
(released 2026-11-17), such as [run
45066154109](https://github.com/marin-community/marin/actions/runs/45066154109/job/137342627186).
setup-uv installs the latest uv, and 0.13.9 spells environment markers
differently when it re-locks; for example, it factors a shared
`python_full_version < '3.13'` term out of each fork. A floor bump
rewrote 16 of the 112 top-level resolution markers and markers in 58
package entries, so validate_targeted_lock_change rejected the lock as
changed metadata. Re-locking main once would not hold: uv 0.13.5
rewrites the lock back to the old form byte for byte.

The guard now ignores marker strings, as #9994 made it ignore the lock
format `revision`. It still rejects a change to the version, source,
hashes, or dependency names of any package other than the released
distribution and its requirement owner. Because the guard cannot tell a
respelled marker from one that changes meaning, bump-releases also
compares the lock with markers and reports `markers_changed`. When it is
true, the workflow opens or updates the PR but leaves the merge to a
person. The first update after this lands is held this way, because
main's lock has the form that uv 0.13.8 and earlier write.

The bump also raised the wrong floor for marin-finelog-server, which
moved into the iris controller extra in #10236. `uv add --package
marin-iris` without `--optional controller` kept the extra's old floor
and added a second marin-finelog-server requirement to iris's core
dependencies; the open update PR #8846 has that line. The bump now
writes the floor in place with update_native_requirement, which already
finds it in any section, and runs `uv lock --upgrade-package`. For all
three packages this gives the same pyproject and lock as `uv add` with
the correct section.

With the versions from the failing run, bump-releases raises the
dupekit-native, iris-native, and finelog-server floors under uv 0.13.5
(`markers_changed=false`) and uv 0.13.9 (`markers_changed=true`).

commits.author: ravwojdyla-agent
commits.message:
[finelog] Let a table raise its client buffer and split large sends (#11941)

`LogClient.get_table` now takes `max_buffer_rows` and
`max_buffer_bytes`, the bounds on the rows that wait in a table's queue.
The flush thread takes one request of rows from the queue at a time, of
about 32 MiB, so a queue larger than one request goes out in several
`WriteRows` requests.

Every table had the default bounds of 10,000 rows and 16 MiB, and a
caller of `get_table` could not change them. A producer that writes in
bursts loses rows at those bounds. One process that ran 2,000 scripted
rollouts through the rollout engine in about 2 seconds wrote 32,000
event rows, and 20,000 arrived.

Larger bounds alone move the loss to the server. The flush thread sent
the whole queue in one request, and the server refuses a `WriteRows`
body above 160 MiB or 1,000,000 rows. The client drops a refused
request, so a 180 MB queue of 3,000 rows lost every row. The same queue
now arrives complete in 6 requests and 5.4 seconds on an embedded server
of version 0.2.67.dev39325146809.

The client sizes a request by its estimate of the queued rows, which
counts the characters of a string and 8 bytes for any other value. It
then checks the encoded size and sends a request above 128 MiB as two
halves, so rows that the estimate undercounts stay below the limit. With
the default bounds, 3,000 rows that each hold a 60 kB `bytes` value went
out as two requests and all arrived; as one request of 180 MB they are
refused. A single row above 128 MiB is dropped. A 270 MiB row got a
retryable error from the server's 256 MiB transport limit, and the
client sent it again without end while the rows behind it waited.

The request size sets the throughput. The server acknowledged the first
request to a table in 0.04 seconds and each later one after about 1
second, also for requests of 256 KiB. That matches `MIN_FLUSH_INTERVAL`,
its cap of one sealed segment each second for a table. A request above
the server's 100 MiB segment size skips that wait: a 480 MB queue took
14.3 seconds in requests of 32 MiB and 2.5 seconds in requests of 120
MiB. The target stays at 32 MiB so that the producer holds a smaller
encoded copy of the rows for each request. `SEND_TARGET_BYTES` is the
constant to raise for a faster drain.

The rows of later requests stay in the queue, so the buffer bounds still
apply to them and `flush` and `close` count them as pending. A queue
within the default bounds that encodes below 128 MiB still goes out in
one request. `Table.close` still waits about 10 seconds for the queue,
and the flush thread stops after that, so a producer with raised bounds
calls `Table.flush` with its own timeout before it closes. `get_table`
raises `ValueError` when a later handle of a namespace asks for other
bounds.

commits.author: ravwojdyla-agent
commits.message:
[rolloutengine] Add order, time and attempt facts to rollout events (#11940)

A `RolloutEvent` now carries `index`, its position in the attempt, and
`emitted_at`, the wall-clock time at which the engine emitted it.
`AttemptStarted` carries the spec's harness and trace mode and the
dataset of the task's source. `AttemptEnded` carries the number of model
turns and the tokens that the attempt spent.

The engine delivers events to the observer from a queue, after the
rollout has moved on, so an observer could not tell when an event
happened. The queue holds 1,024 events for each attempt and drops the
rest. The drop count is in `Rollout.metrics`, which an observer does not
receive. The index counts every emitted event, so a gap in the indexes
that an observer receives is a lost event. The last events of an attempt
can be lost without a gap, so the events are complete when
`AttemptEnded` is among them and every lower index is present.

The start and end fields let an observer that stores events describe an
attempt from those two events, without the `TaskRolloutSpec` or the
returned `Rollout`. No code outside the engine builds these events, and
no production caller passes an observer yet, so no caller changes.

Repair five Reasoning Gym 0.1.25 scorers that award full reward to fixed
incorrect replies. Generated, Nemotron Ultra, and TaskTrove conversions
retain these task families. Shared Verifyit scoring requires finite

propositional example when an entry has no answer. Regressions

null-answer TaskTrove golden regression reproduced a validation failure
before its fix. The affected-test runner passed 326 selected tests and
Harbor's offline suites; Pyrefly reported zero errors. Recipe versions
advance for all three sources, with generated version 3 following
version 2 in #11951. The released validation panel still requires a
separate rebuild to use the repaired grader.

[task-curation] Grade time_intervals rows on any day (#11951)

Compare a regenerated `time_intervals` entry with its recorded entry
without `metadata.start_time` and `metadata.end_time` when the question
holds times only. `reasoning-gym` 0.1.25 parses the two times with
`dateutil`, which fills in the current date, so both fields carry the
day the generator ran. The generated source's grade script compared the
whole entry, so from the next day on it raised `ValueError: Regenerated
entry differs from the recorded entry` for every reply and grading
recorded an infrastructure error. 508 of the source's 1,000
`time_intervals` rows have such a question (task types `time`,
`time_seconds` and `time_ms`).

The question states both times, so the question, the answer and the
remaining metadata still identify the entry. Entries with dates and the
entries of every other task are compared in full, as before. The
generator's `reproducible` flag uses the same comparison as the grade
script.

I encoded the 1,000 entries with `datetime.now()` fixed to 2026-11-04
inside `dateutil`'s parser and ran the grade script's `main()` on
2026-11-20 with each entry's own answer. On main 508 entries raise and
492 print 1.0; with this change all 1,000 print 1.0. The earlier day is
simulated: I did not grade a stored row.

The recipe version moves to 2 because the bundled grade script changes,
so the source's rows get new task ids, and rows converted before this
change keep the old script. The new test in
`test_reasoning_gym_grading.py` is marked `docker` like the others in
that file. I had no grader image, so I ran the file through
`sandbox_grade` with the grading commands as local subprocesses: the new
test ends in an infrastructure error on main and scores 1.0 here.

Fixes #11651

[rl-data] Grade nemotron_if with verifyit's IFEval checks (#11979)

Grade `MarinSkyRL:nemotron_if` with verifyit's IFEval checks instead of
the open-instruct checkers in `skyrl/scorers/ifeval_utils.py`. Each
Nemotron row becomes a list of verifyit constraints, one per IFEval
instruction with the row's non-null arguments, and the grade script
still rewards the fraction of constraints passed. RLVR-IFeval keeps its
conversion, scorer and rubric.

The open-instruct checkers follow RLVR-IFeval's wording, and three of
them fail replies that do what a Nemotron prompt asks: paragraphs
divided by `***`, a `***` divider in a reply with an exact bullet count,
and a `<<title>>` line above `SECTION 1`. verifyit's checks follow the
IFEval wording that these prompts use, and `nemotron_ultra/graders.py`
already grades the Nemotron Ultra instruction rows with them.

On the pinned file (`ab2a40d2`, 56,339 rows), conversion keeps 56,083
rows instead of 54,954. `keywords:letter_frequency`, which had no
mapping, now converts, and 256 rows are rejected because a required
argument is missing or empty. Replies built from each kept row's
arguments and the prompt's wording pass 109,315 of 109,316
single-instruction checks; the exception asks for exactly 0 bullets, so
its literal reply is blank. Replies that combine `***` paragraphs with
bullets pass on all 1,247 rows that ask for both, and a `<<title>>`
above the sections passes on all 582. Over the 54,951 rows both versions
keep, replies that ignore the prompt earn within 0.0001 of their old
mean reward (0.0817 for `yes`, 0.2047 for three unrelated paragraphs). A
blank reply earned 0.0822 from constraints such as "no commas" and now
scores 0.

`language:response_language` stays unsupported: no row uses it, and
verifyit's check passes on a single hint word. The recipe version goes
to 2, so pools built before this change keep the old grading until they
are rebuilt.

commits.message:
[skyrl] Preserve NCCL AllGather in learner processes (#11956)

Permit Ring for NCCL collectives outside all-reduce while retaining Tree for batch-invariant all-reduce in SkyRL's learner processes. The [November 21 SkyRL nightly](https://github.com/marin-community/marin/actions/runs/44925403052/job/136910257408) failed in Grug's two-rank eval test during Megatron optimizer initialization: `all_gather_object` had no available algorithm because `NCCL_ALGO=allreduce:tree` named only the all-reduce function.

The [pinned vLLM initializer](https://github.com/marin-community/vllm/blob/0ac9dcb157ee/vllm/model_executor/determinism/batch_invariant.py#L1142-L1155) overwrites the Ray learner's `NCCL_ALGO` during actor construction. SkyRL now reapplies the Ring fallback after that call, before Megatron creates its process groups. The [targeted H100 rerun](https://github.com/marin-community/marin/actions/runs/44930085809/job/136924588396) passed the original failing case; all three matrix lanes passed. Local affected tests and PR CI passed.

A [full nightly rerun](https://github.com/marin-community/marin/actions/runs/44930544256/job/136927877372) passed the original case and the first four-GPU rollout case, then exposed the same `allreduce:tree` defect inside vLLM's separate inference engine core while profiling a MoE model in `broadcast-32`. That subprocess re-runs vLLM's initializer and fails its own AllGather. Restoring the full lane requires changing the pinned `marin-community/vllm` source setting to include a default algorithm, building a new GPU wheel, and adopting that wheel in Marin. This PR fixes the SkyRL learner side only.

Part of #11955

commits.author: XiaoyuanWang111
commits.message:
[verifyit] Keep the IFEval sentence patterns valid on Python 3.10 (#11952)

Follow-up to #10928, which ended the sentence-mark runs in
`FINAL_MARK_RUN` and `SCRIPT_MARK_RUN` with possessive quantifiers
(`++`, `*+`), which Python added in 3.11. The grader interpreter can be
Python 3.10, where compiling them raises `re.error: multiple repeat`, so
importing `verifyit.modes.ifeval` fails there:
`test_staged_imports_survive_the_grader_interpreter[python-3.10]` fails
on main.

Each run now ends at a negative lookahead for its own class
(`[marks]+(?![marks])`, `[closers]*(?![closers])`), which keeps a run
maximal as the possessive quantifier did. A plain greedy quantifier is
not enough: `SCRIPT_MARK_RUN(?!-\S|\s*$)` would then match the first
marks of a run that ends the text. `SENTENCE_END` and
`UNJOINED_SENTENCE_END` give the same matches and groups as on main for
400,000 random strings over the marks, closers, whitespace, dashes and
letters, and the degenerate-text tests still finish within their
deadlines.

`test_ifeval.py` and `test_grader_interpreters.py` pass, including the
Python 3.10 case that fails on main.

[levanter] Preserve final checkpoints across forced saves (#11960)

Keep the latest checkpoint loadable when the final forced hook follows a
temporary save or a completed-run restart. Promote an existing temporary
checkpoint by changing only its metadata after the pending save
completes. Replace local manifests atomically so an interrupted restart
leaves the prior manifest intact; object-store writes remain direct
because a rename requires a copy and delete.

A CPU crash injection on `main` at `cb991a5` left the default temporary
step and the restarted step unloadable. With this change, the default
step is promoted without a re-save, and the restarted step still loads
after a crash while its replacement manifest is open. Multi-process runs
and a crash during array rewriting on restart remain untested.

Fixes #11959
